page: Amazon Web Services a1.medium is an entry-tier instance powered by first-generation AWS Graviton processors, utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Cortex-A72 microarchitecture. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides one dedicated physical core and one virtual CPU running at 2.3 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache. Memory capacity is fixed at 2.0 GB of RAM, or 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating remote elastic block storage for system and application disks.

Benchmark results demonstrate the functional boundaries of this first-generation architecture. While stress-ng single-core processing achieved a mid-tier score of 1449.88, broader synthetic metrics place the a1.medium in the bottom decile across evaluated cloud servers. Geekbench multi-core recorded 384.0, PassMark CPU reached 381.78, and PassMark memory registered 652.11. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks peaked at 10.43 GB/sec for uncached reads and 5.95 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics reflect these throughput constraints, yielding 0.48 GB/sec in static web serving and 0.47 million operations per second for Redis SET commands.

The primary operational tradeoff of the a1.medium lies in its balance of dedicated resources versus modern execution speed. Because it utilizes a fully dedicated physical core rather than a burstable or shared thread, execution predictability remains stable. However, low raw compute performance, absence of attached local NVMe, and baseline network limits constrain its scope. It serves as a cost-efficient hardware profile strictly for arm64 application development, cross-architecture build verification, continuous integration runners, lightweight background workers, and low-traffic web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.medium is an entry-level cloud server built on the first-generation AWS Graviton architecture with an ARMv8 Cortex-A72 processor. Operating on the AWS Nitro system, it features one dedicated physical core and single vCPU clocked at 2.3 GHz alongside 2.0 GB of system memory. The server provisions no bundled local storage and contains zero GPUs, relying on networked block volumes. Benchmark testing positions the instance in the lower tier for compute and memory throughput, producing a Geekbench multi-core result of 384.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 10.43 GB/sec. Static web throughput measures 0.48 GB/sec with Redis SET throughput at 0.47 million operations per second. With predictable dedicated execution but modest compute capacity, the a1.medium is best utilized for lightweight ARM64 development, CI/CD testing pipelines, small background tasks, and low-concurrency web hosting.
